videos.title: Big AI News: Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Sol, NotebookLM Updates, Muse Charm & More!
videos.ai_tech_id: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) vs GPT-6 Sol (OpenAI) — head-to-head model comparison, plus Gemini Notebook, Grok 4.7/Grok Bot, and Meta Muse/Muse Charm roundup
summary: Paul J Lipsky runs a same-day head-to-head between Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol, since both models launched together, putting each through identical writing, graphic design, and video-editing tasks to see which handles real creative work better.

The video is structured as a weekly AI news roundup built around that comparison: after walking through the three test categories and giving his verdict on results, he moves into a rapid-fire section covering updates to Gemini Notebook, other Google product changes, Grok 4.7 and the new Grok Bot, and Meta's Muse platform alongside its Muse Charm feature, plus recent ChatGPT feature additions.

The framing throughout is practical rather than benchmark-driven: he's less interested in leaderboard scores than in which model an everyday creator or marketer should actually reach for this week, closing with final thoughts on how the Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Sol matchup should shift that choice.

videos.title: Opus 5.5 Just Changed Video Editing Forever (free skills)
videos.ai_tech_id: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) — running inside Claude Code with custom "HyperFrames" editing skills
summary: Nate Herk breaks down a set of one-prompt AI video edits he says are the best he's gotten yet, all produced by driving Claude Opus 5.5 inside Claude Code using a custom skill set he calls HyperFrames, and walks through the exact prompts behind an intro edit, a YouTube showreel, a live-event sizzle reel, three styles of the same product video, and a spec ad.

Rather than treating each edit as a one-off trick, he generalizes the approach into a five-step method he says he follows every time he edits with AI: transcribe the footage, cut it down, plan out the beats, build a reusable skill around the pattern, and have the agent verify its own output before calling it done.

The video positions Opus 5.5 plus HyperFrames as a repeatable production system rather than a novelty demo, and he offers the underlying HyperFrames and a companion website-design skill for free, alongside his usual tool and sponsorship links.

videos.title: Jev vs ChatGPT Luna: 5 to 18x Faster Classification Results
videos.ai_tech_id: Jev AI — specialized classification/routing model, contrasted with general LLMs ChatGPT (Luna) and Claude
summary: Sabrina Ramonov introduces Jev AI, a specialized model built for classification and routing tasks that outputs probabilities instead of generating written responses, and contrasts it directly with general-purpose LLMs like ChatGPT and Claude, which read input, reason over it, and produce text.

She cites a case where an engineer swapped ChatGPT Luna out for Jev on a classification task and reported results 5 to 18 times faster with improved accuracy, framing this as evidence that generating extra tokens is wasted overhead when a workflow only needs a label, score, route, or yes/no decision.

Her practical takeaway is a simple decision rule for builders of AI agent workflows: reach for a general LLM when the task needs language and reasoning, but swap in a lightweight model like Jev for repeated classification or routing decisions such as sorting inputs, choosing a workflow branch, scoring relevance, or detecting spam, risk, intent, or sentiment.

videos.title: GPT-6 Astra Edited This Video in DaVinci Resolve
videos.ai_tech_id: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) via DaVinci Resolve MCP, driven through ChatGPT Codex
summary: Sabrina Ramonov shows the finished result of GPT-6 Astra editing a video directly inside DaVinci Resolve through the new DaVinci Resolve MCP integration, with the whole workflow kicked off from ChatGPT Codex rather than Resolve's native tools.

She lays out the exact setup path: install DaVinci Resolve 21.0.3, open Codex, gather existing photos and videos into a single folder, point Codex at that folder so it has source material, and then describe the desired style in words or hand it reference screenshots and images when words fall short.

The core point is that this workflow requires no blank project or new footage shoot; a creator can start from media already on their computer, describe or visually show the target look, and let GPT-6 Astra execute the edit end-to-end via the MCP bridge into DaVinci Resolve.
